questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) Taylor, Richard, and / (B) Francis plays for / (C) the state / (D) basketball team.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: **B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the singular form of the verb 'plays' is incorrect.
 
• In the given sentence, **subjects 'Taylor, Richard, and Francis'** are **plural**.
 
• When the **subjects are plural**, the **verb should also be plural** (here, **play**).
 
 
• **Example:** *They **play** basketball every weekend*.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the plural form of the verb 'play' should be used in place of the singular form 'plays'.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *Taylor, Richard, and Francis **play** for the state basketball team*.

questions.question:

options.text: Pay a lot of money for something
Give a lot of love and care to someone

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Pay a lot of money for something.

• The idiom **"Pay an arm and a leg for something"** means to pay a lot of money for something. (किसी चीज़ के लिए बहुत पैसे देना)
 
 
• **Example:** He had to pay an arm and a leg for that vintage car.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. Pay a lot of money for something.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** She gave a lot of love and care to the stray dog she found on the street.
 
 
 
• **Pay a lot of attention to an incident** (किसी घटना पर बहुत ध्यान देना)
 
 
• **Example:** The media paid a lot of attention to the recent political scandal.

• **Example:** The story was dramatised for the stage.

questions.question:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

What __most off__ us __want most is to move forward__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'most off'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase 'most off' is incorrect.
 
• The correct phrase should be 'most of'.
 
• 
 
The phrase **"most of"** means the majority or the greater part of something. It is used to refer to nearly all members or elements within a specific group or category.

 
 
• 
 
Example: Most of the students in the class passed the exam.

 
 
 

Therefore, the correct sentence is: ***What most of us want most is to move forward.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Common errors in English often involve the misuse of prepositions such as **'of'** and** 'off'.**

 
 
• **'Of' **is used to show possession, belonging, or origin.

 
 
• For example, "a friend of mine".
 
 
 
• **'Off'** is used to indicate separation or disconnection.
 
 
• For example, "The cat jumped off the table".
